newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - Jan 7.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - Jan 7.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Despite opposition by farm groups, who have demanded the Federal Government extinguish native title on pastoral leases in the wake of the Wik ruling, Acting Prime Minister Tim Fischer yesterday signalled support for a growing view among the States and industry groups that the controversial High Court decision, which found that both forms of land title could exist, be written into Federal legislation rather than overridden by it. Page 1.

The Australian Broadcasting Corporation plans to raise nearly A$14 million over the next two years from the sale of up to eight properties, not including the corporation's prime television site at Gore Hill on Sydney's North Shore. The proceeds from the ell-off will help fund a major technology overhaul during the next five years. The first tranche of properties will include the Sydney television production site at Frenchs Forest and Broadcast House in Melbourne. Page 5.

After two years of battles over the development of the A$100 million Hinchinbrook project, developer Keith Williams has called the stalls a disgraceful indictment of Government in this country and claimed its opponents are using the courts and the nationa media to delay the project without producing evidence that the planned resort development will have any environmental impact. Page 2.

The Australian Society of CPAs, the Institute of Chartered Accountants and the Taxation Institute of Australia increased pressure on the Federal Government yesterday to include tax reform in its program to rewrite the tax act and have called for urgent acions to overhaul the capital gains tax part of the redraft. The three major accounting groups claim Government plans to cut compliance costs for business could not be addressed without substantial reforms to CGT and other problem areas in the tax act. Pge 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Thierry Dubois, of France, and Briton Tony Bullimore, two shipwrecked yachtsmen who had been competing in the controversial Vendee solo around-the-world yacht race, are facing certain death in freezing conditions 2,600 kilometres south of Western Australi unless the navy completes the most ambitious rescue attempted by this country's military. Page 1.

Just eighteen hours after the release of news of the death last Thursday of South Australian cancer sufferer Janet Mills, 52, it was revealed last night no medical specialist was needed to sign the consent form for those wishing to end their lives - a disovery that has increased pressure to have the Northern Territory's controversial euthanasia legislation overturned. Page 1.

Australian Bureau of Statistics figures, released yesterday, and the ANZ Bank's measure of job advertisements show the biggest monthly current account deficit in a year and the weakest demand for labour in almost three years - highlighting two of Australi's worst economic problems - low national saving and high unemployment. Page 1.

The Australian Cricket Board advised the Commonwealth Department of Health and Family Services last night that the Pakistan Cricket Board had agreed that its team would cover the cigarette company logo on its bats for the rest of the Australian tour, savig the ACB from a A$60,000 fine under tobacco advertising laws. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The Howard Government is being confronted with a major economic challenge in 1997, with Bureau of Statistics figures released yesterday showing a worsening in Australia's trade position, with the current account deficit rising to A$1.9 billion in November and the ANZ Bank's survey of job advertisements indicating the worst job prospects in three years. Page 1.

The Higher School Certificate class of 1996 saw 14 top achievers - comprised of eight girls and six boys - scoring the same perfect Tertiary Entrance Ranking of 100. Of the 14, eight attended private schools, five were from Government schools and one studied at an international school in Penang and had never even visited Australia. Page 1.

The RAAF Orion was forced to leave lone French yachtsman Thierre Dupont, 29, who had been competing in the French-organised Vendee Globe single-handed round-the-world race, standing on the upturned hull of his capsized craft in the Southern Ocean in freezng conditions after he failed to receive a life raft dropped to him yesterday. Page 1.

The head of the Environmental Protection Authority, David Harley, said last night he wants Sydney Water to fast-track investment potentially worth hundreds of millions of dollars to protect and clean up Sydney Harbour from pollution before the 2000 Olympi Games. He said organisations involved in operations on the Harbour could face penalties of up to A$250,000 if they failed to care for the waterway. Page 3.
THE AGE

The death of the second person under the Northern Territory's euthanasia act put increased pressure on the Northern Territory Government yesterday to simplify the controversial law, with euthanasia proponent Dr Philip Nitschke calling for the threespecialist rule to be changed. However, Northern Territory Attorney General Denis Burke stated last night Nitschke was mistaken in believing there was any need for a specialist to sign the certificate of request. Page 1.

According to the Australian Maritime Safety Authority, Frenchman Thierry Dubois, 29, a yachtsman found by an RAAF plane in the Southern Ocean yesterday, was unable to get a liferaft dropped to him by the RAAF Orion's crew and was still clinging to the uptrned hull of his craft in conditions described as worsening, with winds of up to 60 knots. Page A1.

In a move backed by the Federal Government for a more extensive State visit, the Council of Aboriginal Reconciliation has asked South African President Nelson Mandela to come to Australia to celebrate the 30th anniversary of the 1967 referendum recognising Aborigines as citizens. Page A1.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
